description: Verify that DUT's ICMP Echo Reply IPv4 header carries TTL > 0 — the value chosen by DUT for outbound packets (suggested 64 per RFC 1700; RFC 1122 §3.2.1.7 'TTL must be a configurable parameter')
approach:
[Objective]
DUT picks the initial TTL for its own outbound packets. RFC 1122 §3.2.1.7 says it must be at least 1 (TTL=0 means 'discard immediately') and the default should be > 1 to allow at least one hop. This case checks that the Reply's TTL is non-zero.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ICMP Echo Request

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: Echo Reply
      - TTL > 0   ← key check

[Pass condition]
Reply's TTL field is greater than zero.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_ttl — Reply emitted with TTL == 0 (would be discarded by the very next hop)
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit a Reply within the window

verdicts.Fail_ttl: Reply emitted with TTL = 0 — would be discarded immediately
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit a Reply within the window
